title: Taylor Farms recalls salsa, guacamole on salmonella outbreak, intensifying food-safety fears
excerpt: Taylor Farms said on Sunday it was recalling prepared food items containing jalapenos from retailers, including Walmart, Kroger and Whole Foods in some states.
content_html:
The logo of Taylor Farms Mexico is seen at the company's facilities, in Doctor Mora, Guanajuato state, Mexico, July 20, 2026.

Demian Chavez | Reuters

Taylor Farms is recalling prepared foods containing jalapenos from retailers including Walmart, Kroger and Whole Foods in several states over potential salmonella contamination, the second major foodborne illness linked to the produce supplier in recent weeks.

The California-based supplier said on Sunday it had voluntarily recalled the products, including salsas and guacamole, after being notified that Coast Citrus Distributors was recalling the fresh peppers due to an outbreak that has sickened more than 300 people.

The recall adds another layer of worry for consumers, who have been avoiding fresh greens at groceries and restaurants after Taylor recalled iceberg lettuce due to a cyclospora outbreak that is already among the largest foodborne illness events in recent U.S. history.

Taylor is one of North America's largest producers of salads and fresh-cut vegetables and a key supplier to major supermarket chains and restaurant operators, including McDonald's and Chipotle.

Taylor Farms said in a statement on Sunday that it had stopped sourcing from a farm in Sinaloa, Mexico, identified as the potential source of salmonella. Its products were also recalled from Target, Trader Joe's and Maine-based supermarket chain Hannaford.

The company was already facing heightened scrutiny due to the cyclosporiasis outbreak that has spread through most U.S. states. Health authorities are still investigating the source of that infection, which causes severe diarrhea and can linger for weeks.

"Consumers are likely to avoid all Taylor Farms products for a while. Taylor Farms will have to work hard to change the perception that its products can make people sick. It could take some time," said Joe Feldman, senior managing director at Telsey Advisory Group.

Industry experts say, however, that because much of Taylor Farms' produce is sold wholesale and unbranded, it will be hard for consumers to steer clear entirely of those products. As a result, overall consumer demand for fresh produce has dipped.

Taylor previously suspended iceberg lettuce sourcing and production from central Mexico after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration linked a large cyclosporiasis outbreak to shredded lettuce supplied by the company from a processing facility in the Mexican state of Guanajuato. As of August 5, the company said the regulator had not confirmed positive sample tests for cyclospora on its lettuce.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the FDA said last week they were investigating the salmonella outbreak, which has sickened 345 people across 27 states and led to 36 hospitalizations.

The U.S. investigation into the salmonella outbreak identified restaurants including Chipotle Mexican Grill and Qdoba, a Mexican-style restaurant chain, as having received jalapenos imported by Coast Citrus Distributors. Both restaurants stopped using them, while Coast Citrus recalled the remaining product and notified customers.

Salmonella infections can cause diarrhea, fever and stomach cramps and can be particularly severe in young children, older adults and people with weakened immune systems.

Taylor Farms said it was unaware of any reported illnesses linked to the voluntarily recalled items.

Walmart said in a statement on Monday that it had removed the products from its stores and implemented a sales block at its registers as well as online.

Kroger declined to comment. Target, Whole Foods, Trader Joe's and Hannaford-parent Ahold Delhaize did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

According to NielsenIQ data, U.S. fresh iceberg lettuce unit sales in the four weeks ended July 25 fell 15.3% from a year earlier, following an 11.1% decline in the four weeks ended June 27.

"The cyclospora scare seems to be having an impact on consumer buying habits. Many consumers are avoiding lettuce of all kinds, unless they know the source, such as a local farm," Feldman added.

content_html_zh:
2026 年 7 月 20 日，墨西哥瓜纳华托州莫拉博士的泰勒农场墨西哥工厂的标志。

德米安·查韦斯 |路透社

泰勒农场正在从几个州的沃尔玛、克罗格和全食超市等零售商处召回含有墨西哥胡椒的预制食品，原因是可能受到沙门氏菌污染，这是最近几周与该农产品供应商相关的第二大食源性疾病。

这家总部位于加利福尼亚州的供应商周日表示，在获悉 Coast Citrus Distributors 由于疫情导致 300 多人患病而正在召回新鲜辣椒后，该公司已主动召回这些产品，包括莎莎酱和鳄梨酱。

这次召回给消费者增添了另一层担忧，在泰勒因环孢菌爆发而召回卷心生菜后，消费者一直避免在杂货店和餐馆购买新鲜蔬菜，这已经是美国近代历史上最大的食源性疾病事件之一。

泰勒是北美最大的沙拉和鲜切蔬菜生产商之一，也是麦当劳和 Chipotle 等大型连锁超市和餐厅运营商的主要供应商。

泰勒农场周日在一份声明中表示，它已停止从墨西哥锡那罗亚州的一个农场采购，该农场被确定为沙门氏菌的潜在来源。 Target、Trader Joe's 和缅因州连锁超市 Hannaford 也召回了其产品。

由于环孢子虫病疫情已在美国大多数州蔓延，该公司已经面临更严格的审查。 卫生当局仍在调查这种感染的来源，这种感染会导致严重腹泻，并可能持续数周。

“消费者可能会暂时避开泰勒农场的所有产品。 泰勒农场必须努力改变其产品会使人生病的看法。 这可能需要一些时间，”特尔西咨询集团高级董事总经理乔·费尔德曼说。

然而，行业专家表示，由于泰勒农场的大部分产品都是批发销售且无品牌，因此消费者很难完全避开这些产品。 因此，消费者对新鲜农产品的总体需求有所下降。

泰勒此前暂停了从墨西哥中部采购和生产卷心生菜，此前美国食品和药物管理局将大规模环孢子虫病爆发与该公司从墨西哥瓜纳华托州一家加工厂供应的生菜丝联系起来。 截至8月5日，该公司表示监管机构尚未确认其生菜的环孢子虫样本检测呈阳性。

美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 和 FDA 上周表示，他们正在调查沙门氏菌疫情，该疫情已导致 27 个州的 345 人患病，并导致 36 人住院治疗。

美国对沙门氏菌疫情的调查发现，Chipotle Mexican Grill 和墨西哥风味连锁餐厅 Qdoba 等餐厅收到了 Coast Citrus Distributors 进口的墨西哥胡椒。 两家餐厅都停止使用它们，而 Coast Citrus 则召回了剩余产品并通知了顾客。

沙门氏菌感染可引起腹泻、发烧和胃痉挛，对于幼儿、老年人和免疫系统较弱的人来说尤其严重。

泰勒农场表示，目前尚不清楚有任何与自愿召回的产品相关的疾病报告。

沃尔玛周一在一份声明中表示，该公司已将这些产品从其商店下架，并在收银台和网上实施了销售封锁。

克罗格拒绝置评。 塔吉特 (Target)、全食超市 (Whole Foods)、Trader Joe's 和汉纳福德母公司阿霍德·德尔海兹 (Ahold Delhaize) 没有立即回应路透社的置评请求。

根据 NielsenIQ 数据，美国新鲜卷心生菜销量在截至 7 月 25 日的 4 周内同比下降 15.3%，继截至 6 月 27 日的 4 周下降 11.1% 后。

“环孢子虫恐慌似乎正在影响消费者的购买习惯。 许多消费者避免食用各种生菜，除非他们知道来源，例如当地农场，”费尔德曼补充道。
